text: This capstone's four lessons -- an authorized retrieval assessment, a shipping checklist, a case study, and this review -- pulled on every one of this course's seven earlier chapters, not just the architecture chapter. This lesson walks back through what each one actually contributed, as a decision you watched play out.

Chapter 1 set the vocabulary used without re-explaining it -- the OWASP LLM Top 10 and the NIST AI RMF are exactly what Lesson 29's finding and Lesson 30's checklist map back to. Chapter 2 is this capstone's most direct ancestor: prompt injection, and the lesson that input sanitization alone isn't enough, is exactly what Lesson 29 tested for and exactly what ProcureAssist lacked in Lesson 31.

Chapters 3, 4, and 5 each became their own category on the Lesson 30 checklist. Data poisoning and supply-chain risk, model extraction defenses like rate limiting, and adversarial robustness's fail-safe instinct didn't appear directly in this capstone's two companies, but any AI feature either one ships next still has to pass those same gates.

Chapter 6 did the most visible work: securing a RAG pipeline end to end is Lesson 29's subject outright, and agent security -- tool use and the blast radius of autonomy -- is exactly what went wrong for ProcureAssist, whose summarization session could reach a tool it never should have touched. Chapter 7's red-teaming discipline is why Lesson 29 was a structured, authorized assessment instead of ad hoc poking.

This capstone proved that securing an AI application isn't one activity -- it's an authorized assessment, a checklist spanning every attack category in this course, and the discipline to recognize that a model behaving correctly at every step can still produce a real incident without privilege separation and a human in the loop.

AI Security Engineering & Adversarial AI Defense is one of four Expert Specialization courses in this path, alongside Digital Forensics & Malware Analysis, Ethical Hacking, Pentesting & Purple Team, and Enterprise Security Architecture, GRC & Risk Management. All four build on the same Advanced Specialization foundation but not on each other, so from here, any of the other three is a valid next step.
